description_short.value: Tema aluminium cold-rolling mill, majority-owned by SSNIT, idle since 2022 and suspended from the Ghana Stock Exchange since October 2023 for failing to file accounts.
description_short.source: Written by us from GSE PR 351/2023 (suspension of listing status of Aluworks Plc) and the Aluworks Plc report and financial statements for 2021 (GSE PR 208/2022: report of the directors, note 34)

description_full.value: Aluworks Plc runs an aluminium continuous-casting and cold-rolling mill in Tema's Heavy Industrial Area, the only cold-rolling plant in Ghana, making sheets-in-coil, flat and corrugated roofing sheets, discs and other semi-finished aluminium products for the building and household markets in Ghana and West Africa. Its shares have been listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange since 29 November 1996. At the end of 2021 the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) owned 62.6% and Caitlyn Limited, an investment vehicle of the Indian aluminium group Vedanta, 21.9%. The company has lost money every year since at least 2017. Revenue was GHS 99 million in 2021, when the loss was GHS 66 million, and fell to GHS 33 million in 2022, with a loss of GHS 75 million that left equity negative. Since 2019 it has been waiting for a restructuring in which Caitlyn, later MALCO, another Vedanta company, would invest working capital in exchange for majority control while SSNIT converted part of its loans into shares. Deloitte, its auditor, declined to give an opinion on the 2021 accounts because of the doubt over its ability to continue as a going concern. Production stopped in 2022. The Ghana Stock Exchange suspended the shares from 2 October 2023 because the company had not filed audited 2022 accounts or its 2023 quarterly reports; the unaudited 2022 statements are its last filing.
description_full.source: Written by us from the Aluworks Plc report and financial statements for 2021 (GSE PR 208/2022: report of the directors, five-year financial highlights, going concern and subsequent events, independent auditor's report, note 34), the unaudited statements for 2022 (GSE PR 024/2023), GSE PR 351/2023 (suspension), the GSE listed-company page (nature of business, date listed) and Ghana News Agency, April 2025 (plant idle since 2022, restart awaiting SSNIT board approval)
